claims.text: Increasing the Cu content of the FeNiCrCoCu coating by about 5 atomic percent will promote Cu-rich oxide formation during high-temperature sliding.
The Cu-enriched coating will form a continuous Cu-rich oxide tribofilm.
The Cu-rich oxide tribofilm will be thin and adherent.
A Cu-rich oxide tribofilm acts as a solid lubricant during sliding.
The Cu-rich oxide tribofilm mitigates direct metal-metal contact.
The Cu-rich oxide tribofilm reduces adhesive contact during sliding.
The Cu-rich oxide tribofilm reduces abrasive interactions during sliding.
The oxide film alters local stress distribution in the coating.
The oxide film reduces or otherwise modulates local dislocation mobility and activity.
The oxide film reduces severe plastic shear and strain localization beneath the sliding surface.
The Cu-enriched coating will have a lower wear rate than the baseline coating under otherwise identical high-temperature sliding conditions.
The Cu-enriched coating will develop fewer abrasive grooves than the baseline coating.
The Cu-enriched coating will exhibit less intense plastic shear than the baseline coating.
The nominal-Cu baseline FeNiCrCoCu coating forms a less continuous or less effective oxide film than the Cu-enriched coating.
Oxide formation occurs in high-entropy alloys during high-temperature exposure in oxidizing environments.
Rapid oxidation relevant to the proposed mechanism can occur in the 600–800°C sliding regime.
The predicted wear and deformation effects require an oxidizing high-temperature sliding environment.
Under ambient or non-oxidizing conditions, the Cu-rich oxide film will have minimal influence on wear resistance and deformation.
High-temperature oxidation is known to influence wear in high-entropy alloys.
